A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Sparse Optimization work and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–G. The additional reference page and minor layout shifts in v2 do not limit comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original CLIP adaptation experiments in Tables 1–5 and extensive two-layer network experiments and training-trajectory analyses in Appendix G.

after.justification: v2 retains the original CLIP adaptation results, ablations, and two-layer network experiments, including the appendix training trajectories.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same random gradient selection, importance-based moment pruning, aligned second moments, dynamic sparsity support, and parameter updates. The wording edits do not change the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 11 CLIP benchmarks and seven datasets in the two-layer network experiments. The full-data, few-shot, pretrained adaptation, and training-from-scratch scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains CLIP, Adam, LoRA, ReLoRA, GaLoRE, PiSSA, DoRA, and VeRA, and the corresponding appendix comparator sets also match. The newly cited CLIP-Adapter is not added to the reported comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 4 retains the rank-2, 500-iteration baseline settings and SO's density ratio of 0.05%, update interval of 10, and 2000-iteration cap. Learning rates, stopping criteria, architectures, shot counts, and appendix protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: Tables 2–5 retain the same pruning, randomness, dynamic-support, and moment ablations. Appendices D, F, and G retain the same sensitivity tests, overfitting analyses, pruning comparisons, and gradient-rank and loss trajectories.

E5.justification: Table 1 still reports averages over three random seeds. Appendix G retains ten-run means and standard deviations, and the plotted uncertainty displays are unchanged. No statistical procedure or run-count change is reported.

E6.justification: The numerical results and plotted findings match, including appendix results and memory estimates. For example, Table 1 reports the same SO average accuracies of 73.8, 76.6, and 78.9 for 1, 2, and 4 shots. All embedded plot images are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7, sparsity definitions, and memory-scaling expressions are unchanged. The added sentence identifying the learning rate and decay rates after Equation 5 restates information already present in v1's notation and Algorithm 1.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same two sparsity paradigms and claims of improved few-shot generalization and memory efficiency relative to low-rank methods. Local wording changes do not alter their scope.

C2.justification: The explanations of overfitting, model expressiveness, pruning mechanisms, and sensitivity tradeoffs remain unchanged, as does the proposed future evaluation on language models. Explicitly mentioning early stopping in the introduction clarifies an existing argument.

D1.justification: The code-access statement, Algorithm 1, hardware and software specifications in Appendix E, and experimental hyperparameters are retained. Relocating Tables 9 and 10 and repeating symbol descriptions disclose no new implementation information.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to the class-dependent effects of regularization and augmentation and to CLIP-Adapter, and adjusts several introductory citation groups. Its additional VeRA reference duplicates the work already listed as reference 20. The research positioning otherwise remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited capitalization, grammar, terminology, and introductory transition edits, adds a symbol reminder after Equation 5, simplifies affiliation markers, and adds acknowledgements. The narrative and section structure remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v2 slightly reduces the size of the main result tables, moves Table 9 before the Appendix G.1 text and Table 10 before the continuing dataset list, and corrects punctuation in Table 10's caption. Figures retain their content and organization; other differences are local spacing and pagination.

improvement.justification: v2 provides small wording and citation refinements, but its added symbol explanation repeats existing information and its scientific evidence and reproducibility content are unchanged. The duplicate VeRA reference and less natural placement of Tables 9 and 10 offset some editorial polish. These limited changes leave overall paper quality essentially unchanged.
